leftEvidence.role: The event named in public proclamation
leftEvidence.title: Reasoning that the Christ had to suffer

points.label: Action and sequence
points.left: In Thessalonica Paul reasons from the Scriptures over three Sabbaths, explaining and demonstrating that the Christ had to suffer and rise, and identifying Jesus as the Christ.
points.right: Jesus begins to show the disciples that Jerusalem, suffering, death, and rising lie ahead; Peter rebukes him and receives a rebuke.

points.label: Evidence boundary
points.left: This later passage uses Crucifixion language inside its own argument without retelling the complete Gospel event.
points.right: The passage materially bears on the Crucifixion while leaving part of its motive, mechanism, or later significance unstated.

payload.posture: Paul’s synagogue reasoning that the Christ had to suffer can be held beside Jesus’ first explicit disclosure and Peter’s resistance.
payload.tension: Acts summarizes a repeated scriptural argument; Matthew narrates one disclosure, rebuke, and call to discipleship.
payload.title: Scriptural reasoning / first disclosure
